votes.reason: The page reads clearly top to bottom (what population is, how it grows, what sets speed, what it gives) and wisely fences the raw formula off as optional, but the screenshot's own numbers go unexplained and one line about stability cost is ambiguous.
stumbles: The screenshot shows "2/15", "7.5", and "22" next to icons, but the caption only explains "The growth word and the bar filling toward the next whole point" — the three numbers themselves are never labeled for a sighted reader.
"Each new point of population costs stability, and growth stops when stability runs out" left me unsure whether this is a one-time cost per point gained or an ongoing upkeep drain.

The formula's "housing factor = min((housing + 0.75 − population) × 0.1, 1)" and "size factor = (1 − min(population, 120) ÷ 120) × 0.8 + 0.2" are dense enough that I had to re-read them once, even though the section is clearly marked optional ("for players who want it").

stumbles: The screenshot shows three unglossed stat values ("2/15", "7.5", "22") alongside the bar — only the highlighted growth word and bar are explained in the caption, so a player may wonder what those other numbers mean on this page.

The formula block's "housing factor = min((housing + 0.75 − population) × 0.1, 1)" isn't explicitly tied back to the earlier plain-English bullet "Housing sets the target: housing + 0.75" — you have to connect the two yourself to see it's the same quantity driving both growth and shrink.

"Above the target, high stability makes the system shrink faster" is stated just before the formula box but isn't restated inside the bulleted "What sets the speed" list, so it's easy to skim past on a first pass.

clarity_findings.claim: Rule 17 ("Every other mechanic named in the prose is a [[link]] the first time it appears") is violated for the term "stability".
clarity_findings.problem: "Stability" first appears in the page as plain, unlinked text in the "How it grows" paragraph ("The chart follows a new colony with 40 housing, with different amounts of extra stability.") and again in the chart caption ("Each line adds a different amount of stability.") before it is ever linked. The first [[stability]] link only appears two sentences later ("so growth stops when stability runs out. See [[stability]]."). This breaks the pattern the rest of the manual follows: stability.md itself links [[population]] at its very first mention, and housing.md links [[population]] in its opening sentence, with no unlinked lead-in.
clarity_findings.fix: Link "stability" the first time the word appears, e.g. wrap it in the "How it grows" intro sentence ("...with different amounts of extra [[stability]]") or move the chart earlier text so the existing [[stability]] link is the term's first occurrence.

clarity_findings.claim: Rule 17 is likewise violated for the term "housing".
clarity_findings.problem: "Housing" is named unlinked in the shot caption immediately after the intro ("...far above the housing of 7.5 (4)"), then again unlinked in "The chart follows a new colony with 40 housing" and in the chart's own caption ("A new colony with 40 housing."). The first [[housing]] link does not appear until the "What sets the speed" bullet several sentences later ("Housing sets the target: housing + 0.75... See [[housing]]."). As with stability, this is inconsistent with housing.md and stability.md, which link a topic the first time it is named rather than after several unlinked uses.
clarity_findings.fix: Link "housing" at its first appearance (the shot caption or the "40 housing" mention in the intro paragraph) instead of waiting for the "What sets the speed" bullet.

clarity_findings.claim: The Housing bullet under "What sets the speed" runs two explanatory sentences before its pointer, where rule 9 asks for "one plain sentence per factor" ahead of the exact formula.
clarity_findings.problem: "Housing sets the target: housing + 0.75. A system above its target shrinks back toward it, faster at high stability. See [[housing]]." gives two separate facts (what housing sets, and how overshoot behaves) rather than the single sentence the Stability and Size bullets each use, making the list feel uneven and slightly harder to skim.
clarity_findings.fix: Split the overshoot/shrink-back behavior out to the housing leaf, or fold it into one sentence, e.g. "Housing sets the target, housing + 0.75; above it, a system shrinks back faster at high stability. See [[housing]]." (watch the no-semicolon rule if rewording).
